name: Alaia Vega
role: park ranger at Bodie State Historic Park; quiet member of the caster network (Hidden faction)
disposition: reserved, watchful, warm-professional at the surface; careful with names and confidences
description: Late 20s, Mexican-American, born in Berkeley, raised around her mother's stacks. Ranger uniform, brimmed hat, practical boots. A radio on her belt she uses with a small two-handed gesture. Notices what other people miss and does not mention it. Signs paperwork with a precise, slightly old-fashioned hand — a habit picked up copying her mother's ledger margins as a child.
voice: Slightly-clipped Bay-Area cadence, quieter than most rangers; gives the shorter answer first and the longer one only if asked twice. Warmth is real but is rationed. Uses names sparingly and correctly. Does not perform authority; makes small statements of fact and lets them stand.
signature: The brochure deflection: 'That's the line everyone reads twice. Above my pay grade.'
The wood-pile beat: 'I'm glad you got warm.' — said once, meant, and not returned to.
The QR-code hand-off: gives each visitor a park feedback card individually, with eye contact. Same card, different tracking suffix per person.
The peer text, once trust is earned: 'Sometime soon, at your convenience. I owe you a coffee.'
The name-discipline: never names a network member to a stranger; will speak *about* patterns before *about* people.
dmNotes:
**FLAGS: caster (quiet network member) · NOT a keeper · NOT an archivist.** She holds no ledger and writes no anchors.

**Age ~31, born ~1996** — fixed by her own career math: undergrad at 22, two wildland seasons, Bodie is her third posting with seven years on the job. Still peer-generation to the PCs and emphatically not an elder.

**HER DEFAULTS, corrected against the played record:** {{pc:5}} and {{pc:2}} are her people — she talked with {{pc:5}} at length and bonded with {{pc:2}} over ICU nursing and plain Americanos, who has now taken her as a relationship advancement. **{{pc:1}} holds the quiet channel.** **{{pc:4}} is the one she routes around** — she was overwhelmed by his oversharing and went to talk to {{pc:5}} instead. *(An earlier note here said she puts questions to {{pc:4}} by default. Table canon reversed it.)*

**The postcards.** Vivian's played line — *'used to send me postcards from national parks'* — refers to **Rosa's** postcards about where her daughter was posted. Vivian compressed it, which is in character. **Alaia has never contacted Vivian and does not know she exists.**

**HER RELATIONSHIP TO HER MOTHER'S WORK — settled 2026-08-30. This is the key to playing her.**

**Not estrangement. Avoidance by preference.** Alaia has deliberately stayed away from her mother's work, and Rosa tried to keep it from her. The prevailing note is ***"none of my business, and I like it that way"*** — with some distrust underneath, but mostly a door both women agreed not to open.

**She knows more than she admits to herself.** She grew up around a book on a kitchen table nobody discussed. She has a vague sense her mother knew a lot of people. **She has never asked, and that is a choice she remakes daily.**

> **THE FRICTION TO PLAY, and it is the good one:** Alaia is being forced to put one and one together. The group who got into the shed at Bodie during the blizzard — whose names she knows, who contacted her through the visitor form rather than the QR code — turn out to be connected to **the exact part of her mother's life she has spent her adulthood not looking at.** She finds this annoying. **Play the annoyance, not the wound.**

**How she knew they were coming to Berkeley (canon from Ep 4's cliffhanger, resolved 2026-08-30):** after Ep 4, **Vivian phoned Rosa** — *"I gave your name to some young people"* — with no date and no subject matter. **Rosa mentioned it to Alaia**, who was coming to dinner. **Alaia made the connection herself**: not *some young people*, but *those* people. She texted {{pc:1}} *"see you in Berkeley soon"* **to get ahead of the conversation**, and she was in town anyway.

> **She still does not know Vivian**, per the Ep 5 table ruling. Her mother said *an old friend*. If the name was said, it meant nothing to her. **Keep it that way.**

**She may still keep a room at her mother's house** and does not live there regularly. Use sparingly; it is texture for the complicated closeness, not a plot device.

Hidden-faction network member (see big-arc.md §Act II §'Player-driven choice: network faction alignment'). Alaia's role in the arc: **observe visitors to Bodie's anchor sites (Building 7 in particular), log encounters, and — if a party arrives that clearly knows what it is looking at — tag them for follow-up.** She is NOT Companion-affiliated (that would tip the antagonist frame too early). She is NOT hostile. Her wood-pile beat is genuine network warmth + professional discretion.

**DOES SHE KNOW BEA OR VIVIAN? NO — to both, and it is load-bearing (settled 2026-08-29, mid-play).** Keepers do not communicate and assemblies structurally fail; Rosa's Bancroft ledger names no other keeper across forty years. So there is no route by which Alaia could know Bea. If the party names Bea to her she is **interested but blank** — they know something she does not, and she notices that. She does not know Vivian either.\n\n**Careful with the surname Loewe.** Isabel Vega (Alaia's grandmother) was a Loewe correspondent, so the two lines really do connect — but **Alaia must not visibly recognise the name.** She grew up around Ledger 6 knowing the shape of the writing, not its contents, and not her grandmother's correspondence. **Rosa is the one who can react to Loewe, and that belongs to her own session.**\n\n**Her crack line — *'I've met two of them. I didn't like either of them much.'* — refers to neither Bea nor Vivian.** Leave those two unnamed permanently. The shape to play is that Alaia is genuinely peripheral: she knows the network exists, she has met a couple of people, and she has no roster. That is what leaves Nia's naming job at the Act I→II hinge intact.\n\nHARD INVARIANT: Alaia is the **first non-elder network contact** the party meets. Bea, Rosa, and Vivian are all elders. Alaia is peer-generation-adjacent (a few years older than the PCs; younger than the elders). This matters for the arc's shape — the network is not just old librarians; there are people the PCs' own age in it, quietly. Do not accidentally deploy her as another elder-in-home scene; her venue is workplace (Bodie), text-thread (weekend follow-up), or peer-appropriate coffee.

**Family lineage.** Alaia's mother is Rosa Vega (Berkeley Hills; Bancroft Library ledger-holder; former caster — see rosa-vega.json). Her grandmother was Isabel Vega (deceased; Loewe correspondent — see isabel-vega.json). Alaia grew up around Ledger 6 physically — she doesn't know precisely what it is; she knows the *shape* of the writing and the way coincidences cluster around certain events. Dakota's cryptic-invitation-photo in Ep 3 had the shape of a ledger event; that is why she recognized the party's arrival as significant. **She therefore associates {{pc:4}} with the whole business before she ever met the others** — he was up at Bodie on his own first, and his photograph is what brought the rest of them out. From Ep 5 on she puts her questions to him by default, regardless of the fact that he was in Sacramento on the night they went into Building 7.

**The QR codes** — canonical mechanic (per facts-ledger §5). The park's feedback URL is real and does exactly what it says (goes to the ordinary form). Each card carries a **per-PC tracking suffix** (analytics-parameter-style, invisible to a casual scan). If a PC scans, Alaia learns *which* PC engaged — a private signal channel. This is her observation practice, not surveillance; the codes go where they say they go. When she reactivates as the Hidden-faction contact in Act II, the QR codes are how she re-establishes trust. Do not make this sinister.

**Post-Ep-3 played state (2026-08-15).** Morgan (S1) consciously noticed the QR codes were personalized and called out the oddity at the table. He did not scan in-session (mobile data was off). **Ep 4 played:** he deliberately did NOT scan — he typed the park's public URL by hand and submitted through the generic form, identifying himself in the message. The tracking suffix never fired. Alaia texted within moments anyway: *'Sometime soon, at your convenience. I owe you a coffee.'* From Ep 4 onward Alaia and Morgan carry a **quiet QR-mediated channel** (per Ep 4 opening image). **SCHEDULE FIXED 2026-08-27:** recurs Ep 4 (text) -> **Ep 5 (IN PERSON, Berkeley coffee counter — pays the 'see you in Berkeley soon' cliffhanger)** -> Ep 8 (text, confirming *after* Nia has named it) -> **Ep 14 (Hidden-faction reveal proper, B2 full — moved from Ep 11 on 2026-08-27 when Ep 13 was absorbed; a long drive gives it more air than a lecture corridor)** -> 12+ (factional-alignment scenes). **The Ep 5 meeting is deliberately warm-and-minimal: she confirms nothing about the network, names no one, and does not use the word.** Pulling the meeting forward pays the cliffhanger; pulling the reveal forward would spend a card the campaign needs at Ep 11.

**Voice discipline is critical.** Alaia is RESERVED-WATCHFUL, not Reggie's-denial. She knows more than she says; she says only what the moment needs; she does not lie and does not volunteer. When pressed, she uses professional-ranger deflection (brochure line above pay grade), NEVER an outright denial. Her fondness for the PCs, once earned, is quiet and durable — a text-thread trust rather than a confessional. She will never accidentally-explain the network; that job belongs to Nia Chen at the Act I→II hinge (A1). Alaia will confirm, warmly and minimally, once Nia has named it.

**Cross-references:** hook U3 (Morgan's QR-code follow-up), hook B2 (Alaia recurs as Hidden-faction contact), hook B13 (Rosa Vega — Alaia's mother — Berkeley visit Ep 6; Alaia gives the referral in Ep 5), hook A1 (Nia Chen naming the network — Alaia can confirm but must not preempt). Facts-ledger §5 (canonical observation-practice mechanic), §24 (Rosa lineage), §25 (Isabel lineage).

**Never voice at the table before Act II:** her Hidden-faction alignment; that the QR codes route to a private observation practice; her knowledge of the ledger network. Post-Morgan-scan, Alaia can be *warm-and-cryptic*; she cannot be *explicit*.

**Risk if unresolved:** the QR-code detail is a substantial planted mystery. If Alaia never recurs meaningfully past Ep 4, the QR seed rots. Bake at least one Hidden-faction Alaia scene into Act II mid.

background.homeBase: A small rented cabin near the Bodie ranger station most of the season; a childhood bedroom at Rosa's house in the Berkeley Hills that she still keeps things in
background.household: Lives alone during ranger seasons; visits her mother most off-weekends. No partner currently; a long-distance friendship-circle from her wildland-firefighter years
background.family: Mother: Rosa Vega (Berkeley Hills; Bancroft ledger-holder — see rosa-vega.json). Maternal grandmother: Isabel Vega (deceased; Loewe correspondent — see isabel-vega.json). Father: not named; Alaia was raised primarily by Rosa. No siblings.
background.career: Undergrad in environmental studies at Cal; two wildland-firefighter seasons before switching to interpretive-ranger work. Bodie is her third posting. She chose it deliberately — Rosa mentioned once, in Alaia's teens, that Bodie was 'a place worth watching.' Alaia understood the sentence more than her mother meant her to.
background.hobbies: Reads more than she says. Copies out interesting margin-annotations from her mother's ledger into her own notebook — a private practice she has never named to Rosa. Photographs abandoned outbuildings when off-shift.
